text: A DTU bundles compute, memory, and I/O into one number — simple, but you can't scale storage independently or apply an existing SQL Server license. The vCore model separates compute and storage entirely.
Pick a service tier and a DTU count, and sizing is done. The cost is that compute and storage move together, and there's no separate compute price to discount.
This is Microsoft's own diagram comparing the two models — bundled DTU on one side, independently priced vCore compute and storage on the other.
No license, want simple sizing — DTU. Own a license — vCore plus Hybrid Benefit. Need independent storage scaling, or Business Critical or Hyperscale — vCore, since those tiers don't exist under DTU.
License ownership and independent storage scaling are the two real deciding questions. Next up: serverless, provisioned compute, and elastic pools.
